observation.visible_scene: A low-angle, near-waterline view across a calm lake at twilight. Out-of-focus dark rocks sit in the immediate foreground; a clump of reeds rises from the water at the right edge; a thin tree line and a few faint vertical masts/posts mark the far shore under a heavy overcast sky streaked with pale pink and blue bands. The sky's color is mirrored on the water surface.
visible_changes: The water surface is not glass-still: small, slow ripples continuously deform and shift the reflected pink and blue sky patches, most visibly in the left-center foreground, so the bright reflection wavers and reshapes frame to frame without translating as a whole.

A small dark floating object (debris/leaf) on the right-center of the water drifts slowly and steadily toward the foreground over the excerpt, moving from roughly mid-frame height near the reeds down toward the lower-right, while the larger dark stick at the far right edge stays essentially fixed.
The camera framing is static: the horizon, tree line, rocks, and reeds hold constant positions, so the observed motion is on the water, not from camera movement.
The cloud pattern in the sky shows no perceptible drift across the ~2.7 s excerpt.
The overall lighting and color balance remain constant throughout.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause of the floating object's drift (current, wind, or a prior disturbance) is not shown.
Whether the ripples are wind-driven or from an unseen source is not visible.
Events before t=0 and after the last frame are unknown; the drift of the floating object may continue beyond the crop.
uncertain_details: The pinkish shapes moving on the water are reflections of the sky, not separate physical objects; distinguishing reflection deformation from true surface motion is not possible from the frames alone.
The small dark mark on the right may be a single piece of debris or two close marks; its exact identity is unclear.
Any cloud motion is below the resolution of these samples and should not be claimed as present.
